examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Separate graph edges from traversal-forest edges. A forest on n vertices with c components has n−c edges, counting isolated vertices as components. For directed graphs distinguish reachability, weak connectivity and strong connectivity; replacing every directed edge by an undirected edge only tests weak connectivity.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
An undirected forest has 28 vertices and 19 edges. How many connected components does it have?

**Answer: 9.** Every tree component with vi vertices has vi−1 edges. Summing gives m=n−c, hence c=28−19=9. This formula applies because the graph is a forest; a graph with cycles can have additional edges without reducing its component count.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A bridge increases the number of components when removed. An articulation point is a vertex property; the two concepts are not interchangeable.

Exactly n − 1 edges does not imply a graph is a tree unless connectivity or acyclicity is also established.
